cards.b: Transfers thermal energy to the surroundings; temperature of surroundings rises. ΔH is negative.
Takes in thermal energy from the surroundings; temperature of surroundings falls. ΔH is positive.

cards.f: Examples of exothermic and endothermic processes
cards.b: Exo: combustion, neutralisation, respiration. Endo: thermal decomposition, photosynthesis.
The transfer of thermal energy during a reaction. Negative = exothermic; positive = endothermic.
The minimum energy colliding particles must have to react.
Breaking bonds is endothermic (energy absorbed); making bonds is exothermic (energy released).
Products lower than reactants; ΔH arrow points down; Ea is the hump above reactants.
Products higher than reactants; ΔH arrow points up.
Reactions occur when particles collide with at least the activation energy (and enough frequency).
More particles have energy ≥ Ea and they collide more often, so more successful collisions: faster rate.

cards.f: Effect of higher concentration or pressure
cards.b: More particles per unit volume, so more frequent collisions: faster rate.

cards.f: Effect of smaller particle size (surface area)
cards.b: More exposed surface, so more frequent collisions: faster rate.
Increases rate by lowering activation energy; it is unchanged chemically at the end.
Measure the volume of gas produced (gas syringe) or the loss of mass over time.
Steeper gradient = faster rate. Curve flattens when a reactant is used up. Same final amount means same amount of limiting reactant.

short.q: Explain, using collision theory, why increasing the temperature increases the rate of reaction. [3]
short.model: Particles move faster so collide more often, and a greater proportion have energy at least equal to Ea, so more collisions are successful.
points: particles have more kinetic energy/move faster

short.q: Explain why increasing the concentration of an acid increases the rate with marble chips. [2]
short.model: More acid particles per unit volume, so collisions with the marble happen more often.

short.q: Sketch and label a reaction pathway diagram for an exothermic reaction. State the labels needed. [3]
short.model: Reactants at higher energy than products, a hump labelled Ea, and a downward arrow for ΔH (negative).

short.q: State how a catalyst increases the rate of reaction. [2]
short.model: It provides an alternative pathway with a lower activation energy so more particles have enough energy to react.

short.q: Describe how you would follow the rate of reaction between magnesium and acid. [3]
short.model: Collect hydrogen in a gas syringe and record the volume at set time intervals (or measure loss of mass); plot volume against time.
points: at regular time intervals with a stopwatch
